writing.topic: Write a message to a friend inviting them to do something at the weekend. Say what you are suggesting and when, give one reason why, offer an alternative in case the first idea does not suit them, and ask them to answer.
writing.practisePoints[0]: an informal greeting and an informal sign-off
writing.practisePoints[1]: make the suggestion with könnten or sollten (wir könnten …, wir sollten …)
writing.practisePoints[2]: give one reason with weil, and put the verb at the end of that clause
writing.practisePoints[3]: offer an alternative (oder am Sonntag; Wenn du keine Zeit hast, können wir …)
writing.practisePoints[4]: say clearly when and where you are meeting
writing.scoringCriteria[0]: the suggestion is a suggestion, not an order: könnten, sollten or Hast du Lust …? rather than a bare imperative
writing.scoringCriteria[1]: the message says what, when and where without the reader having to guess
writing.scoringCriteria[2]: there is an alternative and a request to reply
help.hook: Invite a friend to something, in German, and have the message corrected.
help.intro: This is a planning message: you suggest something, say why, and leave your friend a way out. You write it here in the box, and the app builds a correction request that carries your own text for your AI to correct. Aim for 200 to 500 characters. Two things earn most of the marks: making the suggestion sound like a suggestion, which is what könnten and sollten are for, and putting the verb at the end of the weil clause. A message that says what, when and where, and asks for an answer, is already a good one.
help.tips[0].title: könnten and sollten make it an invitation
help.tips[0].text: A plan in the plain present tense reads as a decision you have already taken. Könnten softens it to an idea, sollten to a recommendation. Both put the other person in the sentence with you: wir könnten, wir sollten.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: We could go to the swimming pool on Saturday.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: We should set off early, then it is not so crowded yet.
help.tips[0].trap: Keep the umlaut: könnten and sollten are the polite ones. konnten means could in the past, and sollten without the umlaut does not exist as a separate form, so an umlaut missing from könnten changes the meaning.
help.tips[0].check.q: Which one invites rather than decides?
help.tips[0].check.why: könnten offers an idea; the present tense states a plan and the imperative gives an order.
help.tips[1].title: weil sends the verb to the end
help.tips[1].text: A reason with weil is a subordinate clause, so its verb moves to the very end: weil das Wetter schön ist. If there are two verbs, the finite one goes last of all: weil ich arbeiten muss.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I am suggesting Saturday, because I have to work on Sunday.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Do come along, because it is sure to be fun.
help.tips[1].trap: denn keeps the normal order and weil does not: „…, denn ich muss arbeiten“ but „…, weil ich arbeiten muss“.
help.tips[1].check.q: Ich kann nicht, weil ich keine Zeit ____.
help.tips[1].check.why: In a weil clause the verb comes last, after the object.
help.tips[2].title: Four things a plan must say
help.tips[2].text: What, when, where, and what to do if it does not suit. A message missing any of the four makes your friend write back just to ask. Offer the alternative with oder or with wenn: oder am Sonntag, wenn dir das besser passt.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Shall we meet at seven at the main station?
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: Or we go on Sunday, if you have no time on Saturday.
help.tips[2].check.q: What is missing from: „Hast du Lust, ins Kino zu gehen? Liebe Grüße“?
help.tips[2].check.why: The invitation is there, but your friend still has to ask what day and what time.
help.tips[2].visual.moves[1].label: When
help.tips[2].visual.moves[3].label: Ask back
help.remember[0]: Suggest with wir könnten or wir sollten, never a bare imperative.
help.remember[1]: weil sends the verb to the end; denn leaves the order alone.
help.remember[2]: Say what, when, where, and offer one alternative.
help.remember[3]: Close with Sag mir bitte Bescheid, then Bis bald or Liebe Grüße and your name.
help.exam: A short message that invites someone and proposes a time is one of the written tasks the A2 certificate sets, and the everyday use of könnten.
help.mistakes[0].why: The first version decides for your friend; könnten invites them.
help.mistakes[1].why: In a weil clause the finite verb goes last.
help.mistakes[2].why: Without the umlaut it means we were able to, in the past.
help.mistakes[3].why: The sign-off starts a new line and takes no comma after it.
